categories.main_business_segments: Under Armour operates primarily in four geographic segments: North America, EMEA (Europe, Middle East, and Africa), Asia-Pacific, and Latin America. The company’s principal business activities are the development, marketing, and distribution of branded performance apparel, footwear, and accessories for men, women, and youth. Apparel is the largest segment by revenue, followed by footwear and accessories. The company also generates a small portion of revenue from licensing arrangements.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Under Armour’s products are engineered with proprietary performance technologies such as HEATGEAR®, COLDGEAR®, UA Iso-Chill™, UA RUSH™, UA SMARTFORM™, and UA STORM™ for apparel, and cushioning platforms like Charged Cushioning®, UA Flow™, HOVR®, and UA Micro G® for footwear. The company focuses on technical fabrications and advanced materials, with product development driven by internal teams and manufactured by third-party contract manufacturers. Sourcing is global, with a concentration in Asia, and quality assurance is maintained through rigorous supplier standards and ongoing evaluations.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company serves a broad range of customers, including national, regional, independent, and specialty wholesalers and distributors, as well as direct consumers through its own retail stores and e-commerce platforms. Key end markets include athletes at all levels, sports teams, and consumers with active lifestyles. No single customer accounts for more than 10% of net revenues, and the company targets both performance and casual use occasions.
categories.geographic_coverage: Under Armour operates globally, with North America (primarily the United States and Canada) accounting for about 60% of net revenues, and EMEA, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America collectively representing the remaining 40%. The company has a significant retail and distribution presence in the U.S., Europe, China, South Korea, Australia, and Mexico, and utilizes third-party logistics providers and distributors in other international markets.
categories.supply_chain_position: Under Armour is positioned downstream in the supply chain, focusing on product design, branding, marketing, and distribution rather than raw material production or primary manufacturing. The company outsources manufacturing to unaffiliated contract manufacturers and manages a global supply chain for finished goods distribution to wholesale and direct-to-consumer channels.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include driving premium brand growth, expanding direct-to-consumer and digital channels, and enhancing operational efficiency through restructuring and cost management. Innovation remains a core focus, with ongoing investment in performance technologies, sustainable materials, and digital consumer engagement. The company is also executing a restructuring plan to improve financial and operational efficiencies and is investing in sustainability initiatives across product and supply chain.
categories.revenue_model: Under Armour generates revenue primarily through the sale of branded apparel, footwear, and accessories via wholesale (58% of FY25 net revenues) and direct-to-consumer channels (40%), including owned retail stores and e-commerce. Licensing arrangements contribute a small portion (2%) of revenue, allowing third parties to produce and sell products under the Under Armour brand.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include Nike, adidas, PUMA, and lululemon athletica, all of which have strong global brand recognition and, in some cases, greater resources. Under Armour competes on brand image, product performance, and selective distribution strategies, but faces intense competition from both global and regional brands, as well as private label offerings from retailers. The company positions itself as a premium performance brand focused on innovation and athletic authenticity.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, Under Armour reported net revenues of $5.16 billion, a decrease of 9.4% year-over-year, and a net loss of $201 million. The company experienced revenue declines across most regions and product categories, with gross margin improvement offset by higher operating expenses and restructuring charges. The company is currently in a restructuring phase, aiming to return to profitable growth and improve operational efficiency.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Under Armour emphasizes making athletes better through innovative, high-performance products engineered for comfort, mobility, and climate adaptability. The brand differentiates itself with proprietary technologies, a focus on athletic authenticity, and a commitment to sustainability. The company’s selective distribution, strong athlete and team partnerships, and digital engagement further reinforce its premium, performance-oriented value proposition.
